note_tweet.text:
How has the share of children born outside of marriage changed?

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), a group of 38 mostly high-income countries, brings together data on family life and family policy in its Family Database, which covers its members, EU countries, and some partner countries.

One of its indicators is the share of children born outside of marriage, meaning births where the mother was not legally married at the time. The OECD collects these figures from national statistical offices and Eurostat.

In 1970, fewer than one in ten children were born outside of marriage in 20 of the 25 countries with data for that year and 2023. The share has risen in all 25 since then — in Spain, it went from 1.4% to 50%.

Most countries don’t have long-term figures on how many couples live together unmarried, which makes this indicator one of the few ways to follow that change over decades.

We recently updated the chart with the OECD’s release from October 2025. For most countries, the data used to end in 2020 and now goes to 2023, and to 2024 for five of them. Colombia is in the data for the first time, from 1998 onward, and has the highest share of all. In 2023, 87% of births there were to mothers who weren’t married.

(This data update was led by @redouad.)

note_tweet.text:
a few months ago I was extensively testing codex/claude code on the public demo of ARC-AGI-3; then astra came, obliterated the benchmark and I lost the interest

originally, I started testing it, because I was tired of the misleading "Humans score 100%, AI <1%" narrative from the ARC Prize team; it also completely failed at tracking the pace of the AI progress

I've never shared the results of those tests so here you go

what I tested:
- openai models with codex or ant models with cc
- agents were sandboxed, had no internet access, all games were independent
- agents were free to use the tools (e.g. create code)
- prompt is a variation of PRO-LONG
- agents could batch multiple commands per call; this drastically speeds up testing and reduces the costs; this has a small downside that the agent has in practice fewer turns to "think"
- I've used the same scoring (RHAE) and the same action limit (5x of human baseline) as the official ARC-AGI-3 does

some caveats:
- runs were performed at various moments, using different versions of codex/cc; this means that quite often, used agent harness might be much more recent than the model
- at least since Opus 5 / Astra 6, models generally have a very good understanding of ARC-AGI-3 env; 
- variance is high, but the relative order of models should be more or less stable
- remember that this is the public demo and the verified benchmark uses private games; that being said, those two should be very close and in general I saw no signs that models have memorized the public games

graphs:
#1: RHAE vs release date; you can see the steady improvement of the models here; ARC-AGI-3 was released soon after gpt 5.4
#2: RHAE vs cost (per game); official testing had astronomical costs (20-100x higher than mine); honestly I don't know how they generated such costs - batching & code execution doesn't fully explain the difference
#3: RHAE vs official RHAE; both values are on the public demo; you can see how little correlation there is between ARC Prize official "minimalistic harness" and a realistic use with a regular coding harness (e.g. codex/cc)

one thing maybe worth mentioning is that I had a ton of additional runs testing variations of prompts, context limits, reasoning level and few other properties; pretty much all of those things made no significant difference on the results

imho the only thing worth mentioning was that apparently a big part of the generated code was used for parsing the visual input from games; I experimented a bit with creating a special limited language for parsing the visual input and when agents were limited to using it, they were nearly on par with runs that had full access to code generation

unfortunately some notable models are missing (fable, opus 4.6 & 4.7), but I've moved on to testing other things  so I'm definitely not revisiting this benchmark

CoWoS, the packaging that holds today's AI chips, was once a joke inside TSMC :))

Shang-yi Chiang, a former TSMC co-COO, says he proposed a packaging unit and Morris Chang approved it quickly. But CoWoS was too expensive. 

A Qualcomm executive told him over dinner the price had to fall to about one cent per mm2. Chasing that cost led to InFO.

Now read the slide shared by Rohan here. A scanner can print only 858 mm2 at a time. In 2024 TSMC's package held 3.3 of those. The roadmap goes to 14 in 2028, about 12,000 mm2, with 20 HBM stacks.

So the thing we buy is no longer a chip but a package :))

My bet is the next hard question is how we cool 12,000 mm2.

note_tweet.text:
i think quantum risk is usually plotted with only one curve.

how fast the machines improve.

the latest @quipnetwork research reminded me there is another curve moving in the opposite direction:

how much machine the attack actually needs.

better hardware pushes capability upward.

better algorithms and error correction can pull the required resources downward.

that distinction matters.

a security plan built only around “quantum computers are still too small” assumes the target stays still while hardware catches up.

it doesn’t.

the attack itself can become cheaper.

so for me, the useful signal is not raw qubit count alone.

watch both sides of the gap:

what the machines can do
and what cryptanalysis now requires them to do
when those curves converge, the timeline can compress without anyone building the giant machine people originally imagined.

that makes post quantum planning less about predicting one breakthrough.

it’s about tracking a moving distance.

1960年代生育高峰期出生的人口正全面进入60岁退休区间，且随着实施渐进式延迟退休政策，退休结构与养老金支撑面临重大压力。

由于育龄妇女总量正在急剧减少，未来10年的年出生人口也大约会锁定在 700-800万上下。

中国史上最大退休潮来了，未来14年，平均每天6万人退休。

数字是按出生人口推的：1962到1975年，3亿多人扎堆出生，现在开始扎堆到岁数。

有人整理过养老口号的变迁：八十年代说“政府来养老”，九十年代改成“政府帮养老”，后来变成“养老不能靠政府”。

口号越来越含蓄，是因为账越算越清楚。

我们的养老金是现收现付——现在交钱的年轻人，养现在领钱的老人。

以后的你，要靠以后的年轻人。

可以后的年轻人，一年比一年少。

所以延迟退休落地了，灵活就业也被动员参保了。

再看领钱这头：最低的一个月一百多，高的一个月一两万。

养老金体系怎么应对？说到底就三个字：谁交钱。
